stories.headline: OpenAI's Codex lead announces global usage reset on day 6 of his pledge
stories.standfirst: Thibault Sottiaux posted "Day 6/ Reset" and promised a global reset by end of day, six days into his pledge to ship a daily Codex improvement or reset everyone's limits.
body: Thibault Sottiaux, whom the Taiwanese outlet Inside describes as OpenAI's Codex lead, posted "Day 6/ Reset" on X late on Saturday, 10 October, UTC. About 20 seconds later he added: "Global reset by EOD. May the tokens do good things for you." At the time we read them, the first post had about 7,100 likes and the second about 2,200. OpenAI has published no changelog entry for the reset that we could find.

The posts refer to a pledge Sottiaux made on 4 October. According to Nerdschalk and Inside, he wrote that over the next 28 days the team would each day either ship one clear improvement for most Codex and Work users, or ship a full reset. Outlets disagree on the end date. Neither early write-up names an improvement shipped under the pledge, so days one to five are unclear.

Nerdschalk's explainer says a full reset refreshes the five-hour and weekly Work and Codex allowances and shifts the weekly reset date, without raising plan limits. It describes three forms: banked resets users apply themselves, automatic ones, and purchased instant resets offered to some Plus and Pro users. Sottiaux's posts do not say which kind this is, and the same outlet notes no reset under the pledge had been confirmed when it wrote.

Separately, TestingCatalog posted a screenshot of what it says is a new Codex setting, "Allow Codex to use resets", in the Usage & billing section. Per the text TestingCatalog quotes, Codex could use a reset when a user explicitly asks during a conversation and has 10% or less of their limit left, and resets are never used automatically. OpenAI has not confirmed the setting, and TestingCatalog's reports are unconfirmed until a company ships.

Inside frames the pledge as a response to competition from Anthropic's Claude Code, and says Codex's weekly active developers passed 4 million in mid-2026; the outlet gives no source for that figure here, and we have not verified it. Nobody else has yet reported on the day-6 reset itself, and the details of who gets it and when remain to be confirmed.

stories.headline: Developer behind free Adobe clones releases open-source Office copies
stories.standfirst: Brandon Thomas of ArtCraft has published WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft, free Rust rebuilds of Microsoft Office. The company says GridCraft already covers 513 of Excel's 523 functions.
body: Brandon Thomas, the developer behind ArtCraft, has published three open-source rebuilds of Microsoft Office apps: WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft. Tom's Hardware reported the release on Sunday, 11 October, and the commentator mark_k posted about it the same day. Thomas earlier published free alternatives to Photoshop, Premiere and Lightroom, which PetaPixel covered on 7 October.

According to Paul Thurrott, who wrote about the project on 9 October, all three are described as clean-room reimplementations in pure Rust. He says ArtCraft claims WordCraft is about 87 percent complete on ribbon commands and 62 percent on real feature parity, and that DeckCraft is in early development. Version 0.3.0 of each is listed on GitHub, according to Thurrott.

GridCraft has the most detail public. Its GitHub wiki describes a spreadsheet that reads and writes XLSX, with native builds for Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD and a browser build via WebAssembly. The project says it has 500-plus functions, PivotTables, 17 chart types and dynamic arrays, and is dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0. It calls itself alpha and puts itself at about 50 percent ready for real work.

The wiki also says every command can be driven through an MCP server, a command-line tool or a JSON control channel, so coding agents can operate the app. Those figures are the project's own estimates, and we have not tested the software. Coverage of the Excel ribbon is put at about 89 percent by ArtCraft, a number nobody independent has checked.

The AI angle is the build method. Mark_k says Thomas used Claude to write the apps, and TweakTown says the Adobe-style tools were built with Claude Opus 5.5. Thurrott states only that the Adobe apps used Claude and does not say the Office apps did. Thurrott also reports that download links appear to have been removed from ArtCraft's website, though the GitHub releases remain.

stories.headline: Yandex says a third data centre is shut after drone attack
stories.standfirst: Reuters reports Yandex shut a data centre near Vladimir after a drone attack, the third in four days. Two of the firm's three AI-model supercomputers are in Sasovo, hit on October 8.
body: Yandex said a data centre in the Vladimir area was shut down after a drone attack, Reuters reported on Sunday. It is the third Yandex site disrupted since Thursday. Reuters' short report did not say who launched the drones, and Ukraine has not claimed responsibility for any of the strikes on the company.

The first was Sasovo, in the Ryazan region, on October 8. Recorded Future News reported that Russian state media, citing Yandex, said the facility was shut down, and that NetBlocks measured connectivity on Yandex's network falling to about 70 percent of normal. Affected services reportedly included Yandex Cloud, Yandex Disk and Yandex Documents.

Al Jazeera, drawing on AFP and Reuters, reported that Sasovo houses two of the three supercomputers Yandex uses to develop its AI models. Yandex did not say whether those machines were affected. On Friday, October 9, Ukrainian drones struck a data centre in the Kaluga region and knocked part of it out of action, Al Jazeera said, citing Yandex.

On Telegram, Yandex warned that the ability to create new resources in its cloud may be limited and advised customers to move workloads elsewhere, Recorded Future News reported. Al Jazeera quoted the company as saying its teams were working day and night to keep services running. Yandex has not said how long the Vladimir site will stay offline.

Al Jazeera quoted Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy as saying Ukraine responds in kind to Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centres, without sharing details. Recorded Future News reported that Russia began hitting Ukrainian data centres in September, including at least six damaged in late September. No outlet has confirmed what was lost at Vladimir.

stories.headline: Nvidia in early talks to buy or deepen stake in Reflection AI, FT reports
stories.standfirst: The Financial Times reports Nvidia is weighing an acquisition, acqui-hire or bigger stake in the open-weights lab it already backs, days after Reflection announced its 501-billion-parameter Beam model.
body: Nvidia is in early talks to acquire, or sharply deepen its stake in, Reflection AI, the Financial Times reported on Friday, according to summaries by Startup Fortune and Data Studios. Startup Fortune says Bloomberg confirmed the report. We could not open the FT piece itself. Neither Nvidia nor Reflection has announced an agreement, and the form of any deal is described as undecided.

Startup Fortune lists the options as an acqui-hire in which Nvidia absorbs Reflection's researchers and licenses its technology, a deal to supply more chips, or a larger equity investment. Data Studios adds a full acquisition. Reflection was valued at $25 billion in its last round, up from $8 billion in October 2025, according to Startup Fortune, which says Nvidia's first cheque was $800 million of a $2 billion raise.

Reflection was founded in March 2024 by Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, both formerly of Google DeepMind, and presents itself as a US open-weights alternative to Chinese labs such as DeepSeek. On 5 October it announced Beam, a mixture-of-experts model with 501 billion parameters, 23 billion active, trained on 23.8 trillion tokens, with a one-million-token context window, per the same reports.

Reflection says Beam matches Z.ai's GLM-5.2 on reasoning benchmarks using three to four times less inference compute. That is Reflection's own approximation and has not been independently verified. Startup Fortune reports Beam trails DeepSeek and Kimi K3 on several benchmarks Reflection published itself. The company says weights and a technical report will follow under Apache 2.0 later this month, and Data Studios says that had not happened as of 10 October.

Startup Fortune also reports that Beam's reinforcement-learning phase ran for four weeks on 10,500 Nvidia GB300 GPUs rented through a $6.3 billion deal with SpaceX's Colossus 2 facility. That figure appears in one outlet only. Price, Nvidia's current stake and any regulatory path are all unknown. Startup Fortune suggests an acqui-hire could avoid a lengthy review, which is the writer's opinion, not reported fact.
